# Terminal 256-ring hypothesis: all-secret nonlinear four-state recurrence gate

**Decision, 15 November 2026, Director #1167.** The original source-derived 32×8 numerical table and 180 authentically known terminal runes do **not** admit an additive GP29 mask generated by **any quadratic or cubic polynomial in its preceding four residues**, even granting every coefficient as a completely unrestricted secret and allowing **1,024 independently oriented original ring layouts per register**. **All 4,096 original-input combinations fail before or at known-residue index40**. An arbitrary two-byte-context mask instead fits almost anything but has **zero predictive coverage** for the withheld outer 76-rune segment. Neither variant recovers unknown p55 plaintext or a source-authenticated key.

This retires one specified four-state nonlinear decoder family, with its stated conditional geometry and base60 byte interpretation. It does not exclude higher-state, alternate-radix, independently keyed, nonpolynomial or non-additive mechanisms.

## Why these inputs and state depth

The original physical LP2 pp49–51 contain **256 printed 2-character number tokens** forming a **32×8** rectangle. Under the documented but still conditional base60-to-byte interpretation, its four concentric rings have exactly **76,68,60,52** cells. Physical p55 has **76 unknown ciphertext runes**; solved p56 has **85 authenticated plaintext runes** and clear p57 has **95 known runes**, giving **180 known terminal symbols** to place in the inner 68+60+52 cells. Source p57's ending urges the reader to shed circumferences and emerge, a plausible but not authoritative cue for examining both inward and outward ring orders. The competing source-visible 256-frame using p53–55 remains a real rival.

A shared earlier algebraic lead factors an original source polynomial into **two GP29 quadratics whose product is quartic**. That gives a motivated state width **four** without proposing an arbitrary new width. Prior [all-secret linear tests](lp2-terminal256-original-inner-separable-gates.md) already reject quartic/order≤88 linear residue recurrences on the same conditional terminal alignment. We test the genuinely new **quadratic and cubic nonlinear feedback** families with every coefficient free.

## Exact nonlinear hypothesis and all-key solution

Let B_t be a printed table byte reduced modulo29 along one source-selected ring traversal. Let P_t be the **known** terminal rune at that position, either p56's genuinely decrypted GP29 followed by clear p57, or the alternative p56 *printed ciphertext* followed by clear p57. This candidate decoder is:

    P_t = (B_t + K_t) mod 29
    K_t = f(K_{t-1}, K_{t-2}, K_{t-3}, K_{t-4}) mod 29

The function f is **any polynomial with total degree at most two or three in four variables over GF(29)**. Its degree-2 case contains **15 free coefficients**; the degree-3 case contains **35 free coefficients**, including constant, linear, repeated-variable and all mixed-variable monomials. No numerical key, IV or feedback coefficients are guessed. The first four source-derived K values are taken as the seed for the known-register fit. Later residues give **176 exact equations**. A streaming GF29 augmented-matrix elimination determines whether *any* coefficient assignment exists; a rank contradiction means every key fails.

Each interior ring may begin at any of four corners and run clockwise or anticlockwise, independently: **8³=512** possibilities. Both orderings of the three inner rings are checked, giving **1,024** per known-register choice. The unknown p55 outer ring is never accessed for fitting. The true p56 plaintext uses the prime/totient key with exactly one nonconsuming literal plaintext-F at local rune index56; its full 85 runes decode to the authenticated original sentence. Positive controls plant separate arbitrary quadratic and cubic four-state generators of the same 180-rune length, and the exact solver accepts both.

## Complete original-input result

| Known terminal register | Polynomial | Completely free coefficients | Ring layouts | Exact original fits | First contradictory known index |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Decrypted p56 + clear p57 | Quadratic | 15 | 1,024 | **0** | **19** in every layout |
| Printed p56 + clear p57 | Quadratic | 15 | 1,024 | **0** | **19** in every layout |
| Decrypted p56 + clear p57 | Cubic | 35 | 1,024 | **0** | **38–39** |
| Printed p56 + clear p57 | Cubic | 35 | 1,024 | **0** | **39–40** |

Contradiction indices are **zero-based positions in the 180 known rune stream**; the first four positions are seed values. Values 19–40 are exact algebraic obstructions, not scores against English, p-values or minimized Hamming edits. An original source-selected quartic-register mask fitting this simple polynomial architecture would give **zero contradictions** on all 176 equations and, in an outward progression, potentially supply the withheld p55 key. None does.

## Why an arbitrary nonlinear state lookup is misleading

The original 256 interpreted bytes contain **161 distinct values**. Consider a much more flexible mask lookup indexed by the consecutive ordered byte pair (B_{t-1}, B_t), with a freely secret GP29 shift for every distinct pair. For the original row-major table and eight uniform original ring directions, **all 75 within-p55 outer consecutive byte-pairs are absent from the 180 known inner-position pair contexts**. The corresponding known-pair dictionaries contain **179 or 180 distinct contexts**, depending on orientation. Thus even if an unrestricted two-byte-context lookup fits 180/180 known runes, it fixes **zero of the 75 unknown outer pair shifts**. Those arbitrary values may each be chosen among all 29 GP symbols, making an artificial decipherment unconstrained. The first unknown position also needs an externally fixed start-state. This is a source-specific **identifiability obstruction**, not a rejection of all nonlinearity.

The calculation avoids a common trap: for any bijective additive key model, decoding the original ciphertext with a fabricated key and then re-encrypting gives an exact round trip by construction. Such an invariant cannot select the historical key.

## Decision and reproducibility

The printed grid cannot be promoted to a GP29 decoder merely because its outer-ring length equals p55's rune count. With original known text, unrestricted four-state quadratic/cubic recurrence coefficients fail decisively; unrestricted byte-pair tables become unconstrained exactly where p55 prediction is needed. A successor should require a **creator-selected decoding operation/initial state from an independent clue**, or a genuinely new finite nonlinear structure that predicts unexamined authentic plaintext before parameter fitting. Retuning ring directions or expanding arbitrary lookup tables is unlikely to advance the solution.

[Single-file Windows-compatible read-only CJS SFT](../sims/lp2_terminal256_nonlinear_fourstate_allsecret_sft.cjs) uses [original-normalized 256 table bytes](../resources/liber-primus/lp2-grid-256.json), the [GP29 manuscript corpus](../resources/liber-primus/lp2-corpus.json), source-frozen 8³ ring orientations and exact GF29 augmented elimination. It validates both planted 180-rune nonlinear positives, both p56 registers, all 4,096 original cases, exact failure-index ranges, and the separate 75/75 unseen-context gate. All the arithmetic results were independently executed in the tool runtime on the exact fetched source JSON before publication; the repository CJS is a separate complete reproducer. No automatic workflow was created.
